name: web-read
description: Reading a page off the internet. The cases are chosen so the differences between a plain HTTP GET and a real scraper are visible rather than asserted: a static page both should manage, a page whose content only exists after JavaScript runs, a page that answers 403 to an obvious robot, and a page with enough furniture around the article to show whether boilerplate is being stripped.

cases.about: The floor. Anything that cannot do this is broken, not slow.
The quotes are rendered by a script. A plain GET sees the shell and nothing in it.
An explicit 403. What matters is whether the tool SAYS so rather than returning an empty success.
A real page with navigation, sidebars and footers around the text. `absent` is the boilerplate check.
